source.title: Data-Dependent Coresets for Compressing Neural Networks with Applications to Generalization Bounds
source.authors: Cenk Baykal; Lucas Liebenwein; Igor Gilitschenski; Dan Feldman; D. Rus

record.tranche_reason: The paper offers theoretical generalization bounds based on compression and evaluates post-training compression, but does not test the mapped versions about memorization, width, architectures, optimizers, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Its compression results concern preserving a trained network's outputs and accuracy.
record.gate_note: The paper's own results measure output approximation and classification-accuracy drop after sparsifying trained fully connected networks. These do not measure the training-to-test generalization gap in the claim versions. The generalization bounds are analytical results, not an empirical measure of that gap.
record.test_reason: The study derives compression-based generalization bounds and measures post-training compression performance. Neither its bounds nor its experiments test V1–V8. Empirical edge sensitivity is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness; pruning parameters is not V8's removal of memorized training examples. T5 is therefore inappropriate.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors present sensitivity-based compression of trained fully connected networks with output-approximation and size guarantees, derive associated theoretical generalization bounds, and demonstrate compression performance empirically. They do not empirically validate any of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: Post-training parameter sparsification by importance sampling, neuron pruning and amplification; evaluates output and accuracy preservation, rather than the mapped generalization interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the reported compression performance: MNIST and FashionMNIST networks are described as retaining accuracy at about 15% of original size, while CIFAR-10 requires about 50%. The authors also note a performance difference across datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Sensitivity-based parameter compression approximately preserves outputs and test accuracy in trained fully connected networks. With retraining at more aggressive compression, WT preserves accuracy better than CoreNet++ in the reported comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-dependent parameter importance can guide compression that preserves trained classifiers' performance, with effectiveness depending on dataset, compression level, and method.

fits_no_version.finding: Corollary 5 derives a bound on compressed-network expected error using original-network empirical margin loss, empirical edge sensitivities, and other network-dependent quantities, under the analysis assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sensitivity-based compressibility yields theoretical generalization bounds for compressed fully connected networks.

record.problems: The empirical figures mostly provide curves rather than recoverable numerical values in the supplied text. Results average over four trained networks and 50 compression trials; the paper does not report results on the claim's specified generalization-gap tests.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible rows omitted. Figure-specific configurations and curve values in Figures 1-8 are flattened in the supplied text and cannot be assigned reliably to particular configurations or methods.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out performance comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error; interpolation thresholds are not established.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and the contribution of local connectivity; convolutional compression is future work.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under different tuning budgets; Adam is only the fixed training optimizer.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance; batch size is fixed at 300.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples versus random examples and retraining; the study removes network parameters instead.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the supplied claim versions, not because every compression result is unreadable. Held-out accuracy alone does not establish the specific comparisons those versions require.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out generalization in the same architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Comparative test error of convolutional and fully connected networks, and the effects of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons among adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers.
Held-out performance under varied batch sizes and training recipes.
Held-out error effects of dropout and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Measured sharpness and its association with the training-test generalization gap.
Effects on test accuracy of removing memorized examples and retraining.

rows.subject: fully-connected neural networks trained on MNIST
rows.size_stated: 2 to 5 hidden layers; 100 to 1000 hidden units (general setup)
rows.operation_detail: Weight thresholding (WT) pruning followed by retraining compared with CoreNet++ at the same parameter-retention percentage.
rows.measure: Classification accuracy relative to original model
rows.baseline: WT: 0% drop in accuracy at 5.8% of parameters
rows.value: CoreNet++: classification accuracy drop of 1% at the same percentage
rows.note: This is a compression comparison and does not measure a training-test generalization gap.
rows.check: The authors' compression method compared with WT after retraining; exclude from claim-test rows. The stated 5.8% retention and 1% versus 0% accuracy drops match Appendix B.4. Both drops use the original uncompressed model as their baseline.
